key_insight: Patient leakage and misaligned labels distorted this benchmark; after correction, no evaluated class-imbalance strategy improved observed mean macro F2 by more than 0.01 over no augmentation.
clinical_relevance: Reliable evaluation of multimodal chest X-ray models requires patient-separated testing and labels aligned to the imaging admission before drawing conclusions about predictive value.
method: Audited record-level splits using an EHR-vector label-lookup baseline and unseen-patient testing.
Traced diagnosis labels to MIMIC-IV admissions and evaluated admission-aligned, rule-refined labels.
Compared imbalance strategies, tuned classifiers, diagnostic history and image embeddings.
evidence_signal: Across 29,083 radiographs from 10,479 patients and eight targets, roughly one-third of radiographs had labels differing from their own admission codes; under corrected evaluation, adding image encoders to diagnostic history yielded no statistically significant F2 gain.
watch_item: Pretraining overlap complicates interpretation: RAD-DINO had seen 96.6% of these radiographs during self-supervised pretraining.
paper_title: Leakage- and Label-Aware Benchmarking of Class-Imbalance Strategies for Multimodal Chest X-Ray and EHR Classification
